issue.body:
reviewer notes (specifically for the migration):
To make reviewing easier, the changes to the type are in a separate PR https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/45176
The approach used by the migration is not perfect but aims to migrate the large majority of use-cases. Shortcomings of this migration are:

* `Route`/`Routes` that need to be migrated are identified by having both "pathMatch" and "path" properties. There is a small risk of this being misidentified. Important to note, in all of g3, there were *0* misidentified objects (objects that were not truly used as an Angular `Route`)
* A small number of routes without an explicit type can and do also define properties that do not exist on `Route`. This currently works because they still conform to the `Route` interface and will satisfy TypeScript when passed to functions. However, they will not satisfy TS when adding the explicit `Route` type to the variable declaration. The migration will create code that won't compile for these cases (less than 5 occurrences in g3). For these, the developer can instead use `const x = {pathMatch: 'full' as 'full'}` or `const x = {pathMatch: 'full'} as const`. This could be the approach used by the migration, but I still believe `const x: Route = ...` is more desirable in all cases where this issue does not happen.
* The algorithm will miss assignments like `const route = condition ? [] : {pathMatch: 'full', path: ''}` since it only walks up from the property until it is not longer in the object/routes array. If that node is not a variable declaration, the migration does not attempt a transform. This only happened 1 time in all of google3.
* The algorithm is not entirely optimized. It walks each child until finding the `pathMatch` property, then walks back up to find the variable declaration. It also doesn't short-circuit further processing of other objects in the `Routes` array. I didn't really attempt to optimize this since migrations are one-offs and I didn't feel it caused exceedingly poor performance. I am certainly open to suggestions/improvements here.

issue.body:
Route.pathMatch only allows `'full'|'prefix'` in reality. This commit
adjusts the type to be more strict and also adds a migration to adjust
existing code.

resolves #37469

BREAKING CHANGE:
The type of `Route.pathMatch` is now more strict. Places that use
`pathMatch` will likely need to be updated to have an explicit
`Route`/`Routes` type so that TypeScript does not infer the type as
`string`.

reviewer notes: migration is in a separate PR (#45084) and has already been run in g3
